questions.history: Register the recording manager as the sole transaction manager. Give the execution fresh job parameters so that it can be created.
questions.prediction: The parent’s Mongo-specific lookup should bypass this recorder. On the merge the repository should use it, and a successful transaction should leave the new execution readable by its ID.

questions.refutation: The merged operation writes metadata without entering the recorder, fails to commit via it, or loses the recorded execution.

questions.history: Supply two instrumented managers, a primary ordinary Mongo manager and a batch-qualified non-Mongo subtype of `PlatformTransactionManager` delegating to the database. Reset both recorders after startup and issue the same repository operation.
questions.prediction: On the merge the batch-qualified manager should handle the repository transaction. The ordinary primary should record no acquisition for it. The returned execution should still be readable.
questions.basis: The qualifier expresses an explicit choice for Batch. A distinct recorder per candidate observes that choice even when either could produce identical Mongo records.
questions.refutation: A primary-only call, both candidates independently acquiring the write transaction, or a missing execution.
